# New content idea — reusable launch and validation template

Copy this file into a separate project. Replace brackets; preserve unknown values as `unknown`, `null` or an unchecked item. This is a planning template, not a completed study, production receipt or permission to publish.

Prepared: [date / timezone]  
Owner: [person]  
Project root: [path / repository]  
Current version: [ID]  
Stage: [discovery / pilot / production / viewer screen / launched / readout]  
Next decision: [specific decision and deadline]

- Content idea: [one sentence]

- Desired audience outcome: [decision or action this helps]
- Owner success criterion: [interest / usefulness / sustainability / paid value]
- Weekly hands-on ceiling: [hours]
- Setup-time ceiling: [hours]
- Cash ceiling: [amount, currency, time horizon, included services]
- Primary platform: [one]
- Secondary platform: [if useful]
- Public launch window: [proposed, not yet scheduled]
- What would make us stop: [precommitted condition]

## 3. Ideal audience and job

**Working ICP:** [specific person in a recognizable situation].

**In their words:** “[original hypothetical phrasing, or a consented actual quote with provenance].”

| Dimension | Hypothesis | Evidence | Uncertainty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Main constraint | | | |
| Discovery routes | | | |

Interview prompts: describe the last time this happened; what did you try; where did you look; what remained confusing; what did it cost in time/money; what would a useful next step have been? Do not begin with a pitch or ask people to validate your desired answer.

## 4. Research plan and source register

Timebox: [hours]. Search scope: [platforms, communities, languages, dates]. Inclusion/exclusion: [criteria]. Access gaps: [specific limitations].

| ID | Kind: evidence/demand/creator/platform | URL/title | Published/checked | Actual access | Finding/question | Scope/limits | Claim/topic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S001 | | | | | | | |

Research five perspectives: engagement/psychology; video/distribution; beginner/customer journey; brand/category; writing. Add domain-specific expertise where necessary. Use original/authoritative support for factual claims. Public demand and creator popularity do not establish correctness or causality.

Culture candidate record: [original URL, dates, platform, observed situation, independent origins, audience connection, counterexamples, useful answer, plain fallback, rights/reuse needs, effort, decision]. Choosing no trend is valid.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Prioritize relevance, supported answer, visible explanation and usefulness within capacity. Record reasons rather than an invented virality score. Sequence orientation before advanced optimization when appropriate.

## 6. Claim map

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Editorial advice and illustrative numbers must be labeled. Review implications in the hook, caption, diagram and thumbnail as well as narration. A general disclaimer cannot repair an inaccurate claim.

## 7. Brand brief

- Mission: [who, outcome, method]
- Vision: [desired lasting change]
- Positioning: [category + audience + useful difference]
- Promise: [bounded, understandable]
- Descriptor: [plain category explanation]
- Name candidates and screening status: [not automatically cleared]
- Voice: [three traits with sentence examples]
- Humor / emotional tone: [what it targets and how it serves the audience]
- Colors/type/layout tokens: [values, licenses, accessibility checks]
- Reusable visual objects: [3–6]
- Character role, if any: [problem participant / demonstrator / companion / none]
- Asset/voice provenance and rights: [actual record]
- Category/meaning confusion to test: [specific possible misunderstanding]

Test category, expected value, recall and meaning before preference. Identify owner-selected options separately from audience-tested options. If using a character, define identity consistency and test its contribution to the lesson and production effort.

Experimental controls remain separate from scheduled episodes unless the protocol explicitly says otherwise.

## 11. Production and technical setup

Canonical content location: [path]. Configuration/tokens: [path]. Source register: [path]. Narration: [provider/retained source]. Rendering: [toolchain]. Dependencies/fonts: [versions/licenses]. Output/review/archive paths: [paths].

Choose specs for the format: [resolution, frame rate, codec, audio, caption size/lines/rate, text margins, contrast, supporting formats]. Verify current uploader overlays rather than trusting inherited margins.

Record exact setup/check/render/package commands after inspecting the implementation. Distinguish network generation from local retained-asset rendering. State command side effects and unresolved dependencies. Keep credentials in private configuration and out of command arguments/manifests.

Provider lifecycle: reserve authorized budget → submit once → retain request ID → reconcile unknown state → retain accepted output/hash → record actual charge → review. Do not automatically retry an uncertain submitted job.

Porting checklist:

- [ ] Separate project root/runtime store/accounts.
- [ ] Fixed series IDs, paths, data schemas and evaluator assumptions audited.
- [ ] Brand/domain/voice/source assumptions replaced.
- [ ] Three real new-domain fixtures render correctly.
- [ ] Retained-media restoration works without historical fitness directories.
- [ ] Appropriate failure-path tests pass.

Distinguish unit-test passes, automated artifact checks, actual human review and audience observation. Never fill an approval field simply to make a tool pass.

## 13. Experiment card

- Question/hypothesis: [one]
- Decision this informs: [specific choice]
- Primary outcome: [one operational definition]
- Variants: [exact difference]
- Held constant: [script, voice, timing, claim scope, diagram, sources, other factors]
- Package-comparison confounds: [what also changes]
- Eligibility/recruitment/consent: [actual plan and authorization]
- Assignment: [method, retained allocation log]
- Exact stimuli hashes: [files]
- Sample/horizon/stopping rule: [set before results; explain basis]
- Missingness/playback-failure rules: [explicit]
- Instrument order: [unaided meaning/action/limit before ratings/preference]
- Critical-error repair rule: [predefined]
- Analysis: [counts, distributions, uncertainty, exclusions, no cherry-picked outcome]
- Decision threshold: [operating rule, not invented statistical significance]
- Status: [prepared / running / completed / retired; actual observations count]

Side-by-side owner review is not randomized audience evidence. Organic topic comparisons are descriptive. Stated follow intention is not an observed follow. Playback estimates are not telemetry.

## 14. Metrics and decision rules

Primary observation window: [hours]. Collection grace period: [hours]. Diagnostic windows: [separate]. Raw export storage: [path]. Metric definitions/source: [current official references].

| Gate | Prelaunch threshold | Basis | Required source | Actual result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mature releases | | | | unknown |
| Adequate exposure | | | | unknown |
| Attention | | | | unknown |
| Useful responses/actions | | | | unknown |
| Comprehension | | | | unknown |
| Critical-error review | | | | unknown |
| Representative production labor | | | | unknown |

GO: [all required conditions, bounded next investment].  
ITERATE: [repairable condition, one change, next horizon].  
NO-GO: [adequately observed failure or capacity failure after simplification].  
INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE: [missing inputs, bounded extension, final investment decision].

Freeze rules before first publication. Keep platform denominators separate and missing values unknown. Preserve low-exposure episodes, raw exports, exact windows and intervention notes. Do not sum overlapping snapshots or change a target after seeing results.

## 15. Measurement forms

Observation: episode ID, platform, post ID, media version/hash, published/observed timestamps, reporting window, duration, available native metrics, source export and missingness reason.

Viewer test: pseudonymous participant ID, eligibility, assignment/first exposure, media hash, takeaway/action/limit, pass/critical error, optional ratings and playback issues.

Response coding: episode/platform, anonymous responder token, date, paraphrase, category, rationale, deduplication scope.

Labor: date, batch, task, start/end, active minutes, unattended minutes, revision reason, source record. Cost: provider/request, currency, actual charge or unknown, retries/failures, accepted output.

Privacy/retention: [what is collected, where contact/consent mappings live, access, retention/deletion]. Aggregates must reconcile to underlying records; empty templates are not observed data.

Accounts/access status: [verified date or user-reported]. Restore steps: [exact instructions]. Tested recovery scope: [what actually passed].

Completed: [facts]. Proposed: [plans]. Retired: [history]. Unknown: [gaps]. Next three actions: [owner, output, acceptance condition].

Final handoff check:

- [ ] Recipient can identify the current audience, promise and next decision.
- [ ] Every scheduled episode has script, sources, caption, asset and owner/status.
- [ ] Exact completed media can be opened without regenerating it.
- [ ] Source restore inputs and tool requirements are included or explicitly located.
- [ ] Manifest hashes, nested archives and critical links were verified.
- [ ] Secrets/private identities are excluded; account setup is explicit.
- [ ] Experiment thresholds and data gaps are preserved honestly.
- [ ] The next operator can distinguish creative preference from audience evidence.
